title: Online news ecosystem dynamics: supply, demand, diffusion, and the role of disinformation
screen_reason: Complex-systems study of the Italian online news ecosystem (Dec 2019 - Aug 2020) that monitors the Supply (posts published by 411 AGCOM-listed news outlets on Facebook and Twitter, filtered to 14 keywords) and the Diffusion (shares/retweets) of that output, with sources split into Reliable and Non-Trustworthy by professional fact-checkers. Table 2 gives the Non-Trustworthy post counts against verbatim platform totals, so the share of outlet output coming from Non-Trustworthy sources is extractable on both platforms (CONTENT).

estimates.ground_truth_detail: Source-level annotation supplied with the AGCOM (Italian Authority for Communications Guarantees) database of Italian news outlets; Non-Trustworthy status assigned by professional fact-checkers. 81 of 411 monitored sources are annotated Non-Trustworthy. No inter-annotator reliability reported; the authors note the source-based methodology follows Grinberg et al. (2019).
estimates.moderator_quote: To analyse the news Supply, we rely on a list of news outlets provided by AGCOM, the Italian Authority for Communications Guarantees, which covers the main leaders of information in Italy during the time span under analysis (AGCOM 2018). The list includes traditional newspapers, online-only news outlets, information agencies, TV, radio websites, and scientific sources. Moreover, the data have specific annotations on Non-Trustworthy sources.
estimates.notes: CONTENT, not SHARING: 'Supply' is the outlets' OWN published output, i.e. all items that exist from these producers, not what an audience shared. Numerator 155,737 and denominator 2,112,678 are both verbatim (Table 2 and Methods text), so this is an exact part/whole share, R8-compliant. Denominator is doubly restricted: only the 411 AGCOM-listed outlets, and only posts containing one of 14 keywords (beirut, calcio, coronavirus, elezioni, Eurovision, lotto, meteo, Morricone, Papa, playstation, Roma, Sanremo, sondaggi, Viviana), hence denom_selection=curated. The AGCOM list deliberately includes Non-Trustworthy outlets (81 of 411 sources), so this is the share of a curated leader ecosystem's output, not of the Italian web. confidence=medium for that reason. population_scope=professional because the producers are professional news outlets, not individuals.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) DIFFUSION (sharing) shares NOT extracted, R8 judgement call for the adjudicator. Table 2 gives Non-Trustworthy shares/retweets and Reliable shares/retweets, but the TOTAL diffusion volume is never stated in the text, so the denominator would have to be formed by summing the two table rows - a cross-category sum, which R8 forbids. The arithmetic, if the review allows an exhaustive two-category partition: Facebook 11,225,099 / (121,108,643 + 11,225,099 = 132,333,742) = 8.48% of shares; Twitter 2,102,646 / (6,291,579 + 2,102,646 = 8,394,225) = 25.05% of retweets. Substantively this is the paper's most striking pattern - Non-Trustworthy outlets supply ~7.7% of tweets but attract ~25% of retweets - and would be two SHARING (content_share) rows if permitted. I left them out because the denominator is not verbatim; the Supply rows I did keep have verbatim denominators. (2) SHARE OF SOURCES not extracted: 81 of 411 monitored news sources (19.7%) are annotated Non-Trustworthy (both counts verbatim). This technically fits 'share of websites classified unreliable', but the 411 are a hand-curated AGCOM list of Italian information leaders into which Non-Trustworthy outlets were deliberately included, so the figure describes the list's composition, not any ecosystem prevalence; extracting it would inject a meaningless 19.7% into the pooled distribution. (3) No CONCENTRATION row: the paper discusses 'leader nodes' and clustering of Non-Trustworthy sources but never pairs a top-X% of users/sources with a share of activity (R1 unsatisfied). (4) All the paper's headline quantities are correlations, not shares: Pearson/Spearman between forces (Fig. 2, 7, 8), semantic similarity medians (minimum 0.66 between Demand and Diffusion on all sources of Twitter, Fig. 6), Spearman coefficients of force similarity against NT supply/diffusion share (Table 1: -0.32 to -0.57), and supply-proxy validation correlations (Table 3: Pearson 0.791 Facebook, 0.861 Twitter). (5) Demand is measured as Google Trends search volume on an arbitrary scale and carries no misinformation share.

rob.design: Observational digital-trace study of Italy, December 2019 - August 2020. Supply = posts by a curated list of 411 Italian news outlet profiles from the AGCOM database (traditional newspapers, online-only outlets, agencies, TV/radio sites, scientific sources), restricted to content containing 14 selected keywords; 2,112,678 Facebook posts (CrowdTangle) and 1,410,711 tweets (official academic API). Diffusion = shares/retweets of those posts. Demand = Google Trends daily search series for the same keywords, absolute-scale procedure, unknown multiplicative factor. Misinformation is source-level only: 81 of the 411 outlets annotated Non-Trustworthy by professional fact-checkers in the AGCOM data; no claim-level verification, no inter-annotator reliability reported, no false-positive validation. Keyword set is acknowledged as non-exhaustive ('the conclusions we draw cannot be considered to be valid for the whole system'), and the authors list expansion to other countries and timeframes as needed. Analysis: Augmented Dickey-Fuller stationarity with 1,000-reshuffle null model, and a smooth-bootstrap conditional-independence (Transfer Entropy) causality test with B = 1000, lag 7 days, Holm-Bonferroni correction. Data and code publicly available.
